stories.title: China has gained pace in the space race by recovering rockets – but can it relaunch one?

en.title: China has gained pace in the space race by recovering rockets – but can it relaunch one?
en.summary: China is pursuing reusable rocket technology as part of its strategy to become a major space exploration player, though the US firm SpaceX currently leads in this field with over 600 missions using reusable rocket boosters.

stories.title: US families ramp up efforts for loved ones’ release from China ahead of Xi’s visit

en.title: US families ramp up efforts for loved ones' release from China ahead of Xi's visit
en.summary: A Chinese-American scientist was arrested at Beijing airport in October 2024 and has remained detained for over 670 days, with his family unable to contact him or know his whereabouts.

stories.title: 中方反对在安理会强推恢复对伊朗制裁

en.title: China opposes pushing restoration of Iran sanctions through UN Security Council
en.summary: China's UN representative stated opposition to forcing through the Security Council a resolution that would restore sanctions against Iran following a vote on extending an expert panel's mandate.

stories.title: 中国海军第48批护航编队访问孟加拉国

en.title: China's 48th naval escort fleet visits Bangladesh
en.summary: A Chinese naval escort fleet arrived in Bangladesh's Chittagong port on the 17th for a scheduled five-day friendly visit.

stories.title: 俄罗斯第九届国家杜马选举开始投票

en.title: Russia's Ninth State Duma Election Begins Voting
en.summary: Voting for Russia's ninth parliamentary election commenced on September 18 in the Kamchatka Peninsula and Chukotka regions. This marks the first nationwide parliamentary election since Russia began its military operation in Ukraine in 2022.

stories.title: 美国向我国返还64件（套）文物艺术品和古生物化石

en.title: United States Returns 64 Sets of Cultural Relics and Fossils to China
en.summary: On September 16 and 18, China's State Administration of Cultural Heritage received 64 items of cultural artifacts and paleontological fossils from US authorities in Washington and New York. The returned items include Buddhist sculptures, terracotta figurines, and dinosaur remains.

stories.title: What the China-Nepal floods teach us about crisis communication

en.title: What the China-Nepal floods teach us about crisis communication
en.summary: A Himalayan disaster at the China-Nepal border last month caused widespread destruction, damaged infrastructure, and disrupted communications in remote areas including Gyirong county in Tibet. The incident highlighted challenges in crisis communication during disasters in physically difficult environments.

stories.title: US trade chief pressed Brazil to review Anglo American nickel sale to China

en.title: US trade chief pressed Brazil to review Anglo American nickel sale to China
en.summary: The US Trade Representative requested Brazil reconsider a Chinese state-controlled company's acquisition of Anglo American's nickel mines in exchange for tariff relief. The proposal emerged during negotiations to reduce the 50 percent tariffs the US imposed on Brazilian goods.

stories.title: US approves sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia despite Israeli concerns

en.title: US approves sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia despite Israeli concerns
en.summary: The United States approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth fighter jets to Saudi Arabia. Israel, the only Middle Eastern operator of the jets, expressed concerns about the sale despite efforts to normalize relations between the two countries.

stories.title: Trump says ‘major progress’ made towards US base in Poland

en.title: Trump says 'major progress' made towards US base in Poland
en.summary: US President Donald Trump announced significant progress in establishing an American military base in Poland, following discussions between Washington and Warsaw. Trump indicated that the location of the base would be announced soon.

stories.title: US sanctions boost China’s science-driven innovation by over 70%, study finds

en.title: US sanctions boost China's science-driven innovation by over 70%, study finds
en.summary: Research indicates that US-sanctioned Chinese companies increased their reliance on open-source scientific research for innovation, with patent applications citing scientific literature rising 72 percent over a 12-year period. The study suggests sanctions may have prompted alternative innovation strategies.

stories.title: Pets and personal touches: how China’s luxury hotel market is changing

en.title: Pets and personal touches: how China's luxury hotel market is changing
en.summary: Chinese luxury hotels are adapting to customer preferences for personalization and cultural experiences. Hotel brands are incorporating individualized amenities and touches to meet evolving hospitality expectations in the market.

stories.title: Hong Kong property market gets reprieve on rates, but position remains precarious

en.title: Hong Kong property market gets reprieve on rates, but position remains precarious
en.summary: Hong Kong property market avoided immediate pressure when major banks maintained unchanged prime rates despite the Federal Reserve's rate increase, though analysts warn fragile recovery remains vulnerable to further hikes.

stories.title: Fed rate hike risks worsening China’s economic divide

en.title: Fed rate hike risks worsening China's economic divide
en.summary: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points to combat inflation, with officials indicating additional increases likely this year, potentially widening economic disparities within China.

stories.title: Who’s in control of Japanese monetary policy? Tokyo or Washington?

en.title: Who's in control of Japanese monetary policy? Tokyo or Washington?
en.summary: US Treasury intervention in Japan's currency market on July 31 coincided with a dramatic shift in expectations for Bank of Japan interest rate decisions. Market probabilities for a rate increase at the September 17-18 policy meeting rose from below 30 percent to nearly 100 percent following the joint US-Japan support for the yen.

stories.title: How Hong Kong’s new 5-year plan courts global capital with an eye on market dominance

en.title: How Hong Kong's new 5-year plan courts global capital with an eye on market dominance
en.summary: Hong Kong unveiled its first five-year economic development plan aimed at strengthening its position as Asia's leading financial centre. The strategy includes expanding equity markets, growing offshore yuan operations, and increasing gold trading activities to compete with London.
